item.description: Anglers will help scientists investigate the porbeagle, tope and blue shark to boost knowledge and conservation ‘We have really cool sharks,” says Dr Lucy Hawkes. She is not referring to animals in the rich coastal waters of South Africa or Mexico, but instead talking about the species that live around Britain. Hawkes, an associate professor at the University of Exeter, is co-leading a new three-year project to investigate the lives of three of England’s most vulnerable shark species. “I like the porbeagle, which looks like a baby great white shark,” she says. “Surfers could see one and… Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.

item.description: Permafrost refers to permanently frozen ground. The rock is held together by ice, much like cement binds concrete. However, when the ice thaws, the ground becomes weak and unstable. item.title: Scientists covered 200 square metres of a Swiss glacier with sheep’s wool; early tests found...
item.description: In an innovative approach, Swiss researchers are experimenting with natural wool blankets to mitigate glacier melting. These eco-friendly coverings have shown results comparable to synthetic options during trials. The initiative makes use of discarded sheep's wool, an agricultural byproduct. Although effective in localized regions, it's important to note that this technique alone won't reverse global warming—tackling greenhouse gas emissions is essential for the long-term preservation of glaciers. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Ancient charcoal reveals evidence of wildfires near the South Pole
item.description: A journey back in time to the Late Cretaceous: A swampy rainforest with conifers and tree ferns stretches as far as the eye can see, dinosaurs roam through the misty wetlands, and the climate is mild and warm. The average annual temperature is 12°C (54°F)—around two degrees higher than in present-day Germany. There is plenty of water, too, as dry periods are regularly followed by monsoon-like rainy seasons. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: In 2023, Australia put a 330-square-metre floating wetland on a wastewater lagoon
item.description: Over the course of two years, research revealed that floating wetlands successfully diminished methane emissions by sixty-six percent, alongside notable reductions in carbon dioxide and nitrous oxide levels. The native vegetation on these platforms is crucial in nurturing beneficial microbes that tackle pollutants and gases effectively. This eco-friendly treatment method reveals a significant advancement in wastewater management, with ongoing tests on analogous floating wetlands in regional agricultural dams. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Francia: ¿qué marcará la carrera por la sucesión de Macron?
item.description: Francia afronta el nuevo curso político con la mirada puesta en las presidenciales de abril de 2027. Europa sigue de cerca una campaña que definirá el relevo de Emmanuel Macron en un contexto marcado por la guerra en Ucrania, las amenazas híbridas de Rusia, crisis migratoria, el impacto del cambio climático y una creciente polarización interna. Los sondeos apuntan, por ahora, a un posible duelo en segunda vuelta entre la ultraderechista Marine Le Pen y el líder de la izquierda radical, Jean-Luc Mélenchon. ¿Puede alguien romper ese escenario? ¿qué márcará la agenda?. item.description: After four years dedicated to rewilding, Broughton Sanctuary has successfully documented over 1,700 species. The estate boasts more than 330,000 trees planted, significantly enhancing forest cover. By managing livestock and beavers, diverse habitats are flourishing. Extensive fencing removal has further facilitated wildlife movement. Going forward, plans include reintroducing native species and expanding vibrant wetland areas for richer biodiversity. item.title: New digital tool shows exactly where California's water goes—and how climate change might disrupt it
item.description: Water has always been one of California's most contested resources. For more than a century, battles have raged over how much of the state's water should be diverted to farmland, pumped into cities or used to conserve aquatic ecosystems—and at times, these clashes have even led to violence. The state's water system consists of a dizzying array of reservoirs, rivers, dams and aqueducts, making it challenging even for experts to understand the trade-offs of different management decisions. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: England released beavers into a Dorset woodland in 2025; one year later, their dams had...
item.description: Beavers newly introduced in Dorset have remarkably transformed a woodland area into a flourishing wetland. Through their natural dam-building, these creatures have slowed down water movement, resulting in the formation of deep pools. This ecological shift has rejuvenated the local fauna, reintroducing various native species to the Purbeck region. Additionally, the beaver dams serve to mitigate flooding on nearby roads during heavy rains, highlighting nature’s essential contribution to environmental resilience.
